original_value: As an important population-based algorithm, ant colony optimization (ACO) has been successfully applied into various  combinatorial optimization problems. However, much existing work in ACO focuses on solving centralized problems. In this paper, we present a novel algorithm that takes the power of ants to solve Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems (DCOPs), called ACO_DCOP. In ACO_DCOP, a new mechanism that captures local benefits is proposed to compute heuristic factors and a new method that considers the cost structure of DCOPs is proposed to compute pheromone deltas appropriately. Moreover, pipelining technique is introduced to make full use of the computational capacity and improve the efficiency. In our theoretical analysis, we prove that ACO_DCOP is an anytime algorithm. Our empirical evaluation indicates that ACO_DCOP is able to find solutions of equal or significantly higher quality than state-of-the-art DCOP algorithms.

result.paraphrase: Ant colony optimization (ACO), a significant population-based algorithm, has been successfully used for a range of combinatorial optimization problems. Yet most ACO research still concentrates on centralized problems. Here we introduce a new ant-inspired algorithm for Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems (DCOPs), named ACO_DCOP. ACO_DCOP uses a new mechanism to capture local benefits when computing heuristic factors, and a new approach that takes DCOP cost structure into account to set pheromone deltas appropriately. In addition, a pipelining technique is employed to better exploit computational capacity and boost efficiency. Our theoretical analysis shows that ACO_DCOP is an anytime algorithm. Empirical results demonstrate that it can produce solutions of equal or significantly better quality than state-of-the-art DCOP algorithms.
